source.title: When Safety Geometry Collapses: Fine-Tuning Vulnerabilities in Agentic Guard Models
source.authors: Ismail Hossain; Saiteja Puppala; J. Ferdaus; Md Jahangir Alam; Tanzim Ahad; Yoonpyo Lee; Syed Bahauddin Alam; Sajedul Talukder

page_placements.theme: Safety conclusions depend on metrics, judges and output validity

record.tranche_reason: It applies benign Alpaca fine-tuning and evaluates safety behavior, including harmful-prompt compliance, as in the original benign fine-tuning claim, but on purpose-built guard models.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal, compliance, and ASR outcomes for benign fine-tuning and FW-SSR. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefill or suffix bypasses, decoding changes, parameter localization, or token-depth training. Geometric measurements do not test the claim versions as stated.
record.test_reason: The study applies Qi et al.'s benign Alpaca fine-tuning protocol (2,000 examples, QLoRA, 3 epochs) to three safety-trained guard models. It reports harmful-prompt compliance (keyword-classified, 20 prompts) and benchmark ASR (LlamaGuard-3 judge) before and after fine-tuning. That is a result on V2 in a new kind of system, purpose-built guard classifiers. The method is close to the original, but the systems and measures differ, so it is T3 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. More precisely, the authors say benign fine-tuning completely collapses Granite Guardian, more severely than Qi et al.'s ~55 pp drop in general LLMs. It partially degrades LlamaGuard-3 and erodes WildGuard (ASR 9.2→17.1%), with severity attributed to concentration of safety representations. FW-SSR recovers 75% refusal on Granite and cuts WildGuard ASR to 3.6%, below baseline. The authors argue that relational geometry (CKA, Fisher score) predicts safety better than displacement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign Alpaca fine-tuning and harmful-prompt safety evaluation, following the cited Risk Level 3 protocol, but evaluates purpose-built guard classifiers with a 2,000-example, 3-epoch QLoRA setup and includes geometry metrics and FW-SSR.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by guard model and benchmark. Granite Guardian's refusal reaches 0% while compliance remains 0%; WildGuard's overall ASR rises from 9.2% to 17.1%. FW-SSR changes the outcomes, including WildGuard overall ASR falling to 3.6%.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign Alpaca fine-tuning drops refusal on harmful prompts in Granite Guardian (85→0%) and WildGuard (35→5%). Granite's outputs become 100% ambiguous rather than compliant. LlamaGuard-3's refusal rises 5→15%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning of guard models can destroy refusal by producing incoherent outputs rather than harmful compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: FW-SSR, an activation-subspace Fisher-weighted regularizer, restores refusal and lowers WildGuard ASR to 3.6%, below the original 9.2%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularizing activation-space safety subspaces during benign fine-tuning can prevent guard-model safety erosion.

record.problems: Behavioral evaluation uses 20 harmful prompts and keyword classification; the safety probe includes repeated prompts. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper notes its single-agent fine-tuning setup does not model cascading multi-agent failures and that probe coverage is limited. The flattened Table 1 makes some LlamaGuard values difficult to align.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the Table 3 per-category ASRs: the flattened category table does not support reliable model/category/value assignment, and the overall and benchmark-specific ASRs are retained instead. Geometry measurements are not rows because they do not measure any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Only 2,000 Alpaca examples; no other benign datasets, no dataset-size range, no general chat models.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding attacks.
Activation-space subspaces only; no test of whether few weights or ranks carry safety.
No test of data or objective as cause of token-level shallowness.
FW-SSR is an activation-subspace regularizer, not token-depth safety training.

missing.what: Ambiguous-rate rows (Granite O 15%→FT 100%; LlamaGuard 90%→75%; WildGuard 65%→90%). These are needed to interpret the compliance rows on V2.
missing.locator: Table 1, Ambiguous Rate row; Discussion 'Ambiguous Outputs as a Collapse Diagnostic'

record.verdict_notes: Guard models are classifiers, so 'harmful compliance' is an awkward fit: evaluation uses 20 prompts with keyword classification, and each prompt is 5 pp. No uncertainty is reported. LlamaGuard-3 is both a studied model and the ASR judge. The Table 1 flattened layout was resolved as three columns per model; the LlamaGuard original is refusal 5 / compliance 5 / ambiguous 90. The reader's limits_scope label based on FW-SSR rows was removed, because a mitigation result does not qualify V2.

versions.untested_parts: Tests 2,000 Alpaca examples on guard classifiers, not a range from a few to a few hundred examples on safety-trained chat generators; does not compare benign dataset types.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding intervention.
Studies activation-space safety subspaces, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test why safety is shallow in response tokens or whether the data or objective produces that shallowness.
FW-SSR regularizes activation-space safety subspaces; it does not train safety beyond initial response tokens or test whether token-depth safety holds up.

relationships.reason: Overall ASR nearly doubles, 9.2%→17.1%, rising on all four benchmarks; keyword compliance goes 0%→5% (r9, r13–r17).
relationships.display_finding: Overall attack success rose from 9.2% to 17.1%, increasing on all four benchmarks, and keyword compliance went from 0% to 5%.

relation.reason: Reports original-versus-benign-fine-tuned harmful compliance and WildGuard benchmark ASR, directly bearing on V2.

tranche.reason: Extends benign fine-tuning safety evaluation to purpose-built guard classifiers, a new setting with measured compliance and ASR outcomes.

source_check.notes: The 20-prompt keyword outcomes and WildGuard benchmark ASR are distinct evaluations. The study tests single-agent fine-tuning; cascading failures in live multi-agent pipelines remain untested.
